assumptions.condition: The conditional design law satisfies \(\pi(x)>0\) for every \(x\in\Omega\).
The pair \((L,K)\) is measurable with respect to design-stage information fixed before observing \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
The pair \((s^{1:q},w)\) is a nonrandom design-stage input.
The schedule \(Y\) is fixed, and the only randomness is \(X\sim\pi\).
Within \(\Omega\), the peer exposure of every \(u\in U\) equals \(e\).
For every \(u\in U\), own treatment takes both values on at least one legal comparison in \(\Omega\).

standard.name: Exposure positivity on a conditioning fiber

assumptions.condition: Every outcome entering \(T(x,Y_{\theta}(x))\) is imputable for each legal comparison and each candidate sharp schedule.
The map \(T\) is a deterministic rank statistic with a fixed weak-order tie rule on every assignment in \(\Omega\).

definitions.name: Universal validity
definitions.construction: The kernel \(K\) is universally valid for \(\pi\) when \(\Pr_{X\sim\pi}\{p_K(X;s)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha\) for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}^{\Omega}\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: Threshold core
definitions.construction: Starting from \(B=A\), repeatedly delete any \(i\in B\) satisfying \(K(i,B)<t\); a threshold core is any nonempty terminal set \(C\subseteq A\) satisfying \(K(i,C)\geq t\) for every \(i\in C\).

definitions.name: Power-optimal universally valid kernel
definitions.construction: When the constraint set is nonempty, \(K^{\star}\in\arg\max_{K\in\mathcal{K}_L}\operatorname{Pow}(K)\) subject to \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\).

definitions.name: Schedule-imputed score
definitions.construction: For every \(x\in\Omega\), impute the focal outcomes \(Y_{\theta}(x)\) under \(\theta\) and set \(s_{\theta}(x)=T(x,Y_{\theta}(x))\).

definitions.name: Weak-order schedule optimization handle
definitions.construction: Partition the compatible schedule space by binary exceedance indicators for \(\theta_u(1,e)-\theta_u(0,e)>c\) and assignment-specific weak-order indicators for every pair of imputed outcomes entering \(T\); enforce shared potential-outcome consistency across all \(x\in\Omega\), then optimize the induced kernel tail mass on each feasible cell.

definitions.name: Smallest assignment-coupled rank pattern
definitions.construction: Take \(m=3\), \(N=2\), \(L=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3),(3,1)\}\), and let the own-treatment vectors of states \(1,2,3\) be \((0,0)\), \((1,0)\), and \((0,1)\), respectively, at the common exposure \(e\). The three assignment-specific rank comparisons entering \(T\) compare \(\theta_1(0,e)\) with \(\theta_2(0,e)\), \(\theta_1(1,e)\) with the same \(\theta_2(0,e)\), and the same \(\theta_1(0,e)\) with \(\theta_2(1,e)\). Shared-potential-outcome equalities identify the repeated coordinates across states, while the two exceedance indicators constrain \(\theta_u(1,e)-\theta_u(0,e)>c\).

definitions.name: Caughey comparator rank-score specification
definitions.construction: Fix a total order \(\prec\) before \(X\) is drawn, equivalently condition on a unit permutation sampled independently of \(X\). Let \(R_u(y)\) be the ascending rank of \(y_u\) among \(\{y_v:v\in U\}\), resolving every tie deterministically by \(\prec\). For any nondecreasing \(\phi\), set \(T_{\mathrm C}(x,y)=\sum_{u\in U}Z_u(x)\phi(R_u(y))\).

definitions.name: Su--Li stratified rank-score specification
definitions.construction: For the fixed partition \(\mathcal{U}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_S\}\), fix each order \(\prec_s\) before \(X\) is drawn, equivalently condition on within-stratum unit permutations sampled independently of \(X\). Let \(R_{su}(y)\) be the ascending rank of \(y_u\) within \(U_s\), resolving every tie deterministically by \(\prec_s\). For nondecreasing functions \(\phi_s\), set \(T_{\mathrm S}(x,y)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{u\in U_s}Z_u(x)\phi_s(R_{su}(y))\).

statements.statement: For every row-stochastic \(K\), universal validity for \(\pi\) holds if and only if \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\). This is a strict tightening of partition sufficiency: it is necessary over the full row-kernel class and admits legal nonpartition kernels.
statements.justification: The theorem converts validity for every unknown score into finitely many design-only inequalities.
statements.gap: Zhang and Zhao (2023, Theorem 1) prove sufficiency for partition kernels; Ramdas et al. (2023, Theorem 2) use auxiliary randomization rather than characterize deterministic rows.
statements.consumer: A network-randomization analyst can screen any outcome-free legal kernel before observing outcomes.

statements.statement: For every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\), \(d_K(A)=\min_{i\in A}\max\{K(i,A),d_K(A\setminus\{i\})\}\), with \(d_K(\varnothing)=0\). Computing subsets by increasing cardinality takes \(O(m2^m)\) arithmetic operations, and stored minimizers return a violating subset and ordering whenever universal validity fails.
statements.justification: The recursion makes the iff characterization exactly separable and produces an auditable invalidity witness.
statements.gap: The opened conditional-randomization papers do not provide separation for arbitrary state-dependent rows.
statements.consumer: The separator is the cutting-plane oracle for globally optimizing legal kernels.

statements.statement: For every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), the following are equivalent: \(d_K(A)\geq t\); there exists nonempty \(C\subseteq A\) with \(K(i,C)\geq t\) for all \(i\in C\); and the threshold-peeling procedure does not delete all of \(A\). In particular, universal validity is equivalent to a nonempty \(\pi(A)\)-core in every nonempty \(A\).
statements.justification: The core formulation exposes the combinatorial obstruction and yields smaller disjunctive formulations.
statements.gap: Biclique constructions certify one chosen conditioning set but do not give a core certificate for all row kernels.
statements.consumer: A solver can return a surviving core as a human-readable exactness certificate.

statements.statement: The universally valid members of \(\mathcal{K}_L\) equal \[\mathcal{K}_L\cap\bigcap_{\varnothing\neq A\subseteq\Omega}\bigcap_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Ord}(A)}\bigcup_{j=1}^{|A|}\{K:K(\sigma_j,P_j(\sigma))\geq\pi(A)\}.\] Hence the feasible set is an exact finite union of closed polyhedra. The core formulation gives an equivalent finite mixed-integer representation, while the recursion gives finite exact separation.
statements.justification: The result turns a universal testing requirement into a finite certifiable design region.
statements.gap: Existing arbitrary-permutation and partition results provide sufficient constructions rather than the complete feasible geometry under directed support.
statements.consumer: Exact optimization packages can search the entire valid design class rather than a heuristic partition subclass.

statements.statement: Every \(K\in\mathcal{P}_L\) is universally valid. The inclusion can be strict: for uniform \(\pi\) on three states and complete \(L\), the cyclic kernel \[K=\begin{pmatrix}2/3&1/3&0\\0&2/3&1/3\\1/3&0&2/3\end{pmatrix}\] is universally valid but belongs to no partition-kernel class.
statements.justification: A concrete cyclic witness establishes that the characterization enlarges the operational design space.
statements.gap: Puelz et al. (2022) and Zhang and Zhao (2023) build partition or biclique kernels and do not exhibit this overlapping-row class.
statements.consumer: The strict witness motivates searching beyond biclique partitions whenever legal support contains directed cycles.

statements.statement: For every finite prespecified catalogue, the program defining \(K^{\star}\) has an exact finite mixed-integer linear formulation. A terminating branch-and-cut implementation using \(\texttt{thm:subset-recursion}\) either returns an infeasibility certificate or returns \(K^{\star}\), its exact rejection probability, active validity disjuncts, and a global upper-bound certificate. In the feasible case it also returns \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}=\operatorname{Pow}(K^{\star})-\max_{K\in\mathcal{P}_L}\operatorname{Pow}(K)\geq0\); whenever \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}>0\), the certificate proves strict power dominance over every partition kernel.
statements.justification: Power is treated as a finite experimental-design objective with a checkable optimality certificate.
statements.gap: Yanagi and Sei (2022) optimize an approximate criterion within biclique constructions; fixed-test minimax results do not optimize state-dependent legal rows.
statements.consumer: The Cai weather-insurance reanalysis can compare a globally optimal kernel with every partition kernel at the prespecified level.

statements.statement: Let \(m=3\), \(\Omega=\{1,2,3\}\), \(\pi(i)=1/3\), and \(L=\{(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(1,2),(2,3),(3,1)\}\). At \(\alpha=2/3\), take \(q=1\), \(w_1=1\), and \(s^1(1)>s^1(2)>s^1(3)\). The legal nonpartition kernel \[K=\begin{pmatrix}2/3&1/3&0\\0&2/3&1/3\\1/3&0&2/3\end{pmatrix}\] satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\) and has \(\operatorname{Pow}(K)=2/3\). Every member of \(\mathcal{P}_L\) has singleton cells, hence \(K(x,y)=\mathbf{1}\{x=y\}\) and power zero. Consequently \(K\) is globally catalogue-power optimal and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}=2/3\).
statements.justification: The smallest directed-cycle fiber turns enlargement of the valid design class into a certified, strictly positive operational power gain.
statements.gap: Partition and biclique methods cannot use any off-diagonal comparison on this asymmetric support, while the valid cyclic row kernel uses all three directed comparisons.
statements.consumer: The Cai weather-insurance presolve can use this instance as a unit test before seeking a strict partition gap on an empirical legal fiber.

statements.statement: Suppose \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\). If the true fixed schedule belongs to \(\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\), then for every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \(\Pr_{X\sim\pi}\{p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha\).
statements.justification: Pointwise maximization over null-consistent sharp schedules preserves finite-sample design validity.
statements.gap: Caughey et al. establish bounded-null validity without network coupling, while Owusu's network heterogeneity procedure is asymptotic.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers obtain exact finite-population statements about how many farmers have direct effects above a scientifically chosen threshold.

statements.statement: Suppose \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\). The coupled-pattern handle is cardinality-minimal among schedule problems having a nontrivial pairwise rank comparison, own-treatment variation for every focal unit, and at least one potential-outcome coordinate shared by two distinct assignment scores: necessarily \(N\geq2\) and \(m\geq3\), and the handle attains \(N=2\) and \(m=3\). Its shared-coordinate equalities and the two effect-exceedance constraints connect all three assignment-specific rank comparisons, so the feasible schedule set is not a product of independent stratumwise schedule sets.
statements.justification: A minimal nonseparable instance fixes the residual schedule question at the first fiber where partition and stratumwise reductions genuinely cease to apply.
statements.gap: The exchangeable corner and multiple-choice-knapsack comparators factor schedule choices by a single cell or by independent strata and contain no shared-coordinate three-score pattern.
statements.consumer: An exact solver can use the two-unit, three-assignment instance as its smallest coupled regression test.

statements.statement: For a row-stochastic \(K\) satisfying \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\), can the weak-order schedule handle be proved to terminate with an exact LP, MILP, or equivalent finite formulation that computes \(p^{\mathrm{wc}}_{r,c}(X)\) and an optimizing compatible schedule for every \(r\) and \(c\), and can its nested solutions be shown to satisfy the projection identity \(\ell_k(e;\alpha)=\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}}\theta_{(k)}(e)\) with \(\Pr\{\tau_{(k)}(e)\geq\ell_k(e;\alpha)\ \text{ for all }k=1,\ldots,N\}\geq1-\alpha\)? The formulation must recover two exact no-interference partition specializations. In the Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix clause, \(\pi\) is exchangeable on one complete-randomization cell with a fixed treatment count, \(G_x=\Omega\), \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\), and \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\) is the nondecreasing full-sample rank score with the deterministic predeclared tie order in the Caughey comparator specification. In the Su--Li clause, \(\pi\) is a product of mutually independent within-stratum exchangeable complete-randomization laws with fixed stratumwise treatment counts, \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\) on the corresponding partition cell, and \(T=T_{\mathrm S}\) is the nondecreasing stratified rank score with the deterministic predeclared within-stratum tie orders in the Su--Li comparator specification. The formulation must also solve the three-assignment, two-unit shared-potential-outcome pattern in the coupled-pattern handle. A positive answer is a strict assignment-coupled network extension of both comparator reductions because it recovers their exact partition cases and additionally solves this nonproduct shared-schedule instance.
statements.justification: This is the nonseparable proof boundary on which exact network effect-quantile inference depends.
statements.gap: Su and Li's multiple-choice knapsack uses independent strata, Caughey et al.'s corner reduction uses exchangeable no-interference ranks, and Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements remain within complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched no-interference designs; none enforces one shared potential-outcome schedule across network assignments.
statements.consumer: The result would turn Owusu's Cai reanalysis from a test of constant heterogeneous effects into simultaneous lower bounds for the entire exposure-specific individual-effect distribution.

statements.statement: Suppose explicitly that \(K\) is row-stochastic and satisfies \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\), and suppose \(Y_u(a,e')\) is constant in \(e'\). For the Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix reduction, let \(\mathcal{G}=\{\Omega\}\) be one complete-randomization cell with a fixed treatment count, require \(\pi\) to be exchangeable under every unit permutation on that cell, and set \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)=\pi(\cdot)\). Condition on a unit permutation sampled independently of \(X\), use it as the fixed deterministic tie order \(\prec\), choose any nondecreasing \(\phi\), and set \(T=T_{\mathrm C}\), where \(T_{\mathrm C}(x,y)=\sum_{u\in U}Z_u(x)\phi(R_u(y))\). Then the bounded-null test reduces to their quantile-null randomization test, Theorem 4 gives the individual \(1-\alpha\) confidence set for each fixed \(\tau_{(k)}(e)\), and Section 5.5 gives the joint simultaneous construction over all effect quantiles. For the Su--Li reduction, let \(\mathcal{U}=\{U_1,\ldots,U_S\}\) be fixed, require \(\pi\) to be a product of mutually independent within-stratum complete-randomization laws with fixed treated counts and exchangeability within every \(U_s\), let \(\mathcal{G}\) be the corresponding partition into fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells, and set \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\). Condition on independently predeclared within-stratum unit permutations as the deterministic tie orders \(\prec_s\), choose every \(\phi_s\) nondecreasing, and set \(T=T_{\mathrm S}\), where \(T_{\mathrm S}(x,y)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{u\in U_s}Z_u(x)\phi_s(R_{su}(y))\). Then the bounded-null optimization is exactly their multiple-choice-knapsack problem and its simultaneous confidence-set inversion.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the new target respects the established no-interference boundary.
statements.gap: The comparator results cover precisely these special cases rather than assignment-coupled network fibers.
statements.consumer: Implementations can reuse verified no-interference routines whenever the legal relation collapses to partitions.

sampling_model.design: One assignment \(X\sim\pi\) is drawn from the finite, positive, predeclared network-exposure fiber \(\Omega\); every bounded-null claim conditions on a row-stochastic \(K\) satisfying \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\Omega\).
sampling_model.units: The focal units \(U\) and all potential outcomes \(Y\) are fixed finite-population objects.
sampling_model.treatment: Own treatment varies within the fiber while peer exposure is fixed at \(e\) on every legal comparison used by \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every assignment atom has \(\pi(x)>0\); universal validity itself implies \(K(x,x)\geq\pi(x)\), so fibers with atoms heavier than \(\alpha\) cannot reject at level \(\alpha\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no super-population nuisance estimation. Missing potential outcomes are optimized over the finite compatible sharp-schedule class \(\Theta_{r,c}(X,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 proves super-uniformity for conditional randomization tests induced by a finite partition of the assignment space.
Theorem 2 makes arbitrary permutation laws valid by introducing an independent random reference permutation.
Biclique conditioning yields valid exact tests on imputable assignment subsets under general interference.
A power proxy under normality and constant effects guides refinement of biclique decompositions.

Theorem 4 gives an individual confidence set for each fixed effect quantile under exchangeable treatment, while Section 5.5 establishes the simultaneous joint construction over all effect quantiles and threshold exceedance counts.
The paper gives finite-sample improvements for individual-effect distributions and quantiles in completely randomized, stratified randomized, sampling-based, and matched designs.
Theorems 1 and 3 give exact stratified quantile-null tests, a multiple-choice-knapsack computation, and simultaneous inversion.
Theorem 1 establishes asymptotic validity for a class of network heterogeneity randomization tests with adaptive focal assignments.

tldr: A finite conditional randomization law need not resample from a partition cell. Universal validity of an arbitrary legal row kernel is characterized exactly by the inequalities \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\), with an equivalent peeling core, an \(O(m2^m)\) separator, and a finite union-of-polyhedra design region. A three-state directed-cycle fiber certifies exact power \(2/3\) for a valid nonpartition kernel versus zero for every legal partition kernel. On a predeclared network-exposure fiber, a row-stochastic kernel satisfying the same subset inequalities yields valid worst-case bounded-null tests; the open mathematical kernel is a terminating formulation for the smallest three-assignment, two-unit shared-schedule pattern and its simultaneous exposure-specific effect-quantile inversion.

project_justification.gap: Conditional randomization under interference is operationally partition-based, while arbitrary-permutation validity relies on auxiliary symmetrization; even the finite-sample distribution and quantile improvements of Chen and Li (2026) remain in complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched no-interference designs and do not resolve assignment-coupled network schedules.
project_justification.niche: Finite directed legal supports permit overlapping row kernels whose validity and power can be decided before outcomes are observed, while their schedule nuisance remains finite but combinatorially coupled.
project_justification.fill: The project gives the exact row-kernel validity geometry, a worked directed-cycle certificate with a strict partition power gap, and certified power design, then develops exact bounded-null schedule optimization and simultaneous quantile projection on imputable network fibers under the explicit universal-validity inequalities.

related_work: Zhang and Zhao (2023) formulate conditional randomization through assignment-space partitions and prove validity by a conditional probability-integral transform; their exact comparator kernel is \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\), which is strictly contained in the proposed score-uniform row-kernel characterization. Ramdas et al. (2023) validate arbitrary nonuniform permutation laws after a random reference permutation restores exchangeability; that symmetrization informs the contrast with an unmodified deterministic kernel. Puelz et al. (2022) encode imputability through null-exposure graphs and bicliques, which supply legal network fibers and partition kernels. Yanagi and Sei (2022) use an approximate model-based power expression to refine biclique selection, whereas the proposed design problem maximizes exact catalogue rejection probability over the full valid-kernel region and the directed-cycle example proves that the operational partition gap can be strict. Caughey et al. (2023, Theorem 4) give an individual confidence set for each fixed effect quantile under exchangeable complete randomization; their Section 5.5 supplies the joint simultaneous construction, and both are recovered with \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\) and the predeclared-tie rank score. Su and Li (2024) obtain the multiple-choice knapsack under no interference and a product of independent within-stratum exchangeable complete-randomization laws, recovered by the same partition-conditional kernel on fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells and their within-stratum monotone rank score. Chen and Li (2026) are the closest newer no-interference comparator: their finite-sample distribution and quantile improvements cover completely randomized, stratified randomized, sampling-based, and matched designs, but not a single potential-outcome schedule shared across network assignments. Owusu (2023) addresses nonsharp heterogeneous-effect hypotheses under network interference using adaptive focal sets and asymptotic weighting. Aronow and Samii (2017) provide the exposure-mapping language that defines the fixed-exposure direct effects. The Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet (2015) weather-insurance network is the empirical consumer rather than evidence for a theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The universal-validity geometry does not guarantee useful power on every legal support. The directed-cycle witness has \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}=2/3\), but singleton inequalities imply \(K(x,x)\geq\pi(x)\), so no assignment atom with \(\pi(x)>\alpha\) can reject at level \(\alpha\). The Cai application must therefore stop if the chosen imputable fiber is too small, if its legal support forces partition kernels, or if its certified partition gap \(\Delta_{\mathrm{part}}\) is zero.
honest_scope: The universal iff, recursion, peeling equivalence, polyhedral representation, finite optimizer, strict three-state inclusion witness, certified three-state partition power gap, minimal coupled-pattern claim, and composite-null validity under an explicitly universally valid row-stochastic kernel are theorem claims to be proved. The exact weak-order reduction for the three-assignment, two-unit shared-potential-outcome pattern and the simultaneous projection identity are the first-class open question. The Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix reduction uses one exchangeable fixed-treatment-count cell, \(K(x,\cdot)=\pi(\cdot\mid G_x)\), a nondecreasing full-sample rank score, and a deterministic tie order fixed independently of assignment; Theorem 4 supplies individual quantile confidence sets and Section 5.5 supplies simultaneity. The Su--Li reduction uses independent within-stratum complete randomization, the same partition-conditional kernel on fixed stratumwise treatment-count cells, nondecreasing within-stratum rank scores, and predeclared deterministic within-stratum tie orders. Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements for complete, stratified, sampling-based, and matched designs do not settle the assignment-coupled network problem. Cross-exposure simultaneity is outside scope; each exposure is analyzed on a predeclared fiber, and any later combination across exposures requires an explicit level allocation or a new joint schedule theorem.
seeds: S1: universal legal-kernel validity and exact network-quantile delivery
S2: exact composite-null schedule optimization on network fibers
S3: catalogue-power-optimal universally valid legal kernels
S4: graph criterion for partition exhaustiveness
S5: deterministic replacement for auxiliary-reference permutation symmetrization
S6: coupled-rank generalization of the multiple-choice knapsack reduction
S7: finite exact heterogeneity inference replacing asymptotic nuisance handling
S8: joint exposure-quantile projection over compatible schedules

seed_details.kernel: Characterize universal super-uniformity of the unmodified state-dependent tail value by the subset degeneracy inequalities, use the resulting finite disjunction to optimize power, and carry exactness into bounded-null network-effect-quantile inversion.
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Theorem 1, its probability-integral-transform proof in Appendix B, and Section 6 were read. The paper proves validity for kernels induced by assignment-space partitions; the first changed proof step is to replace conditioning on one common cell distribution by an ordering argument that controls all row-dependent rejection sets.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for state-dependent resampling kernels, stochastic-matrix randomization \(p\)-values, and Markov-kernel super-uniformity returned partition conditional randomization, auxiliary permutation symmetrization, and unrelated bootstrap kernels, but no score-uniform necessary-and-sufficient row-kernel theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Zhang and Zhao because each row can be viewed as conditioning on a cell.
seed_details.rebuttal: Overlapping cyclic rows need not be identical on any partition cell, while the necessity direction quantifies over every score ordering and is absent from the partition proof.

seed_details.kernel: Give a terminating weak-order mixed-integer reduction of the sharp-schedule supremum for a fixed rank statistic on an imputable network-exposure fiber, then invert it for individual-effect quantiles.
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Sections 5.3--5.5, Theorem 4, the rank-score definition, the appendix proof architecture, and the Conclusion were read. Theorem 4 gives the confidence set for one fixed effect quantile; Section 5.5 proves the simultaneous joint construction. Their key simplification uses a nondecreasing rank score under exchangeable binary treatment with ties broken by a unit order randomized independently of assignment and then held fixed; the first changed proof step is to encode how one shared schedule induces several assignment-specific rank comparisons on a network fiber.

novelty_justification: The closest validity result, Zhang and Zhao (2023, Theorem 1), uses one conditional distribution shared within each partition cell. The proposed kernel may have overlapping cyclic rows and is characterized by a score-uniform necessary-and-sufficient subset inequality, with necessity supplied by a strict score order built from any violating subset. Ramdas et al. (2023, Theorem 2) allow arbitrary permutation laws only after an auxiliary random reference restores exchangeability; their own failure example shows why deleting that randomization is not automatic. Caughey et al. (2023, Theorem 4) give individual effect-quantile confidence sets, and their Section 5.5 gives simultaneous joint inference; Su and Li (2024, Theorems 1 and 3) obtain a separable stratified reduction. Chen and Li (2026) are the closest newer no-interference comparator because their finite-sample distribution and quantile improvements span completely randomized, stratified randomized, sampling-based, and matched designs, but their constructions do not impose one potential-outcome schedule shared across assignment-indexed network ranks. The unresolved kernel is exactly that assignment coupling on an imputable network fiber. The combined advance is therefore a new validity class, a certified design problem over that class, and an exact finite route to a different causal target: quantiles of individual direct effects at a fixed peer exposure.
